JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 19-04-2017 at about 05.30 a.m., when she was travelling to Karimnagar, Telangana from Bengaluru in the Orange Travel Bus bearing Regn.No.AR-02-5708, the driver of the said bus who is the first respondent drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and all of a sudden took a 'U' turn near Madanpally Patha Thanda and dashed against the Trailer which was proceeding towards Peddagolkonda.

Due to which, petitioner sustained grievous injuries and thereafter she was shifted to Trident Hospital, Shamshabad, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient for which she has spent a sum of .4,75,000/- towards treatment,
medicines and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and she was doing Tailoring work and earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Orange Travel Bus by its driver.
The respondents being the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondents did not appear before the Tribunal and as such they have been placed as ex-parte.

4. Now the points that arise for my consideration as follows:
POINTS 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 19.04.2017 at about 5.30 a.m., on NH-44, Madanpally Patha Thanda,
when she was proceeding in Orange Travel Bus bearing Regn.No.AR-02-5708, due to rash and negligent driving, the said bus dashed against the Trailer bearing Regn.No.AP-15-TA-7659?

Puli Archana vs Kodati Raju on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164666515/
2
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
5. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 and closed her side of evidence.
6. Heard the counsel for the petitioner.

The petitioner has contended that on 19-04-2017 when she was travelling to Karimnagar, Telangana from Bangalore in the Orange Travel Bus bearing Regn.No.AR- 02-5708,
the driver of the said bus who is the first respondent drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and all of a sudden took a 'U' turn near Madanpally Patha Thanda and collided against the Trailer which was proceeding towards Peddagolkonda and the result of the same the petitioner sustained injuries resulting in fracture of her right leg.

9. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of the Orange Travel Bus bearing Regn.No.AR-02-5708 by Respondent No.1, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 by filing her affidavit in lieu of chief examination, wherein she has reiterated the averments made in the petition with regard to the rash and negligent driving of the offending bus by its driver, about the injuries caused to her, about the treatment taken by her, about the expenditure incurred by her for the treatment etc.

10. In support of her oral evidence, she has produced the documentary evidence such as FIR, copy of first information, translated copy of first information, copy of charge sheet, statement of witnesses,
copy of crime details marked at Ex.P.11 to 15, which establishes the date, time and place of accident and also that the accident is occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus by the respondent No.1.

The Medico-legal certificate, which is marked as Ex.P.16 evidences that the petitioner has sustained an abrasion over her right foot and the same is grievous in nature and the other medical documents such as the Discharge summaries, which are marked as Ex.P.1 & 2 goes to show that the petitioner sustained wedge fracture injury.
From the documents produced by the petitioner it also goes to show that the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.337, 338 of IPC.

The respondent No.1 who is the driver of the offending vehicle, the Respondent No.2 who is the owner of the bus and the Respondent No.3 who is Puli Archana vs Kodati Raju on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164666515/

sentences.text: 3 the insurer of the offending bus did not appear before this tribunal to disprove the case of petitioner.
The evidence of petitioner remains unchallenged.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Orange Travel Bus bearing Regn.No.AR-02-5708 by its driver who is the Respondent No.1 and the result of which the petitioner sustained injuries.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
In view of my finding on Issue No.1 that the petitioner has sustained injuries as a direct result of the accident, she is entitled to claim compensation.
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustaining injury over her right ankle joint.
Ex. P16 to 18 which are the Medical certificates goes to show that the petitioner has been treated for one injury which was grievous in nature.
12. The discharge summary as per Ex.P.1 issued from Trident Hospital discloses that petitioner has taken treatment from 19-04-2017 to 23-04-2017 for a period of 5 days.

The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to her and no evidence on record to say that she has suffered permanent disability and there is no loss of future income due to the alleged disability.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
(i) Towards Pain and Sufferings:- The petitioner has shown to have sustained one grievous injury which is a Wedge fracture D12.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc., it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of .60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:- Regarding treatment and medical expenses incurred etc., the petitioner has taken treatment at Trident Hospital.
The petitioner has produced 29 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.10.
On overall calculation, it amounts to .28,932/-.
One bill produced by the petitioner amounting to .4,500/- is already included in the final bill as such the said bill is not taken into consideration.
Further two more bills are produced by the petitioner in respect of taking a private room in the hospital which is amounting to .12,000/- (each).
Both the bills are one and the same and the bill amount of said .12,000/- is also already included in the Final Bill.
As such those two bills are also not taken into consideration.
On overall calculation of the remaining bills, it amounts to .28,932/-.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for .28,932/- under the head medical expenses.

(iii) Towards Incidental Expenses:- Further for 5 days of hospitalization at Trident Hospital, and for follow up treatment in the said hospital, she requires an attendant,
has traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses,
she has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at .20,000/-.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- under the head incidental Puli Archana vs Kodati Raju on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164666515/
4 expenses.
(iv) Towards Loss of Income during laid down period:-
It is submitted that the petitioner is self employed.
She is giving tuitions and also doing tailoring work and earning sum of .25,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said aspect the petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this Tribunal considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner,
considers the income of the petitioner as .11,000/- p.m. The petitioner has sustained grievous injury and has taken treatment for 5 days as inpatient.
Hence the nature of injury i.e., one fracture sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold period of two months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for two months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of .22,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.

(v) Towards Loss of Amenities and Discomforts:-
The petitioner at her age of about 30 years has suffered grievous injury.

Hence taking into consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of .30,000/-
towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

13. The Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:-
 Sl.No. Heads Amount

1 Towards Pain and Sufferings .60,000/-
 2 Towards Medical Expenses .28,932/-
 3 Towards Incidental Expenses .20,000/-
 4 Towards Loss of Income during .22,000/-
 laid down period  5 Towards Loss of Amenities and .30,000/-
 Discomforts  TOTAL .1,60,932/-
Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for .1,60,932/-.
14.

Now coming to the liability of payment of the compensation to the petitioner is concerned,
though notice is served on the Respondent No.1 who is the driver, Respondent No.2 who is the owner and Respondent No.3, who is the insurer of the offending bus, they have not appeared before this Tribunal to deny the claim of the petitioner or to deny with regard to the validity of the Insurance policy taken by them.
As such respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
The 3rd respondent is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 and 2 in making payment.
Accordingly, Point No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Point No.3:
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .1,60,932/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty Thousand Nine Hundred And Thirty Two only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer over computer, corrected and pronounced by me in open court on this 15th day of June, 2024.)
